newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Seven opposition parties join Zambia poll boycott.
newsitem.headline: Seven opposition parties join Zambia poll boycott.

text.p: Seven opposition parties on Friday joined former president, and now main opposition leader, Kenneth Kaunda in his party's boycott of Zambia's general elections on November 18.

Controversial constitutional changes passed in May by a parliament dominated by supporters of President Frederick Chiluba, block Kaunda from running for president, but his United National Independence Party (UNIP) is free to participate.
Kaunda, president for almost three decades until Chiluba ousted him in Zambia's first free elections in 1991, said on Wednesday neither he nor his party would participate.
"The seven opposition parties have resolved to boycott the elections because of the government's refusal to address their concerns," an opposition spokesman said.
The constitution bans second-generation Zambians and former presidents who ruled for two terms from standing for president.
The parties have also rejected the voters' register, which excludes half the 4.6 million eligible voters in the country.
But government said it would go ahead with elections despite the withdrawal of the parties. About 30 other parties are still running in the race.
"These parties that have decided to boycott the elections are just cowards. They are afraid to face us at the polls," minister without wortfolio Michael Sata told Reuters.
Political analysts said the opposition's decision was a setback for the country's emerging democracy.
"We understand their concerns, but it is a pity they decided to boycott the elections. It is not healthy for the democratic process," German amabassador Peter Schmidt said.
